name: Apalit Libad Fluvial River Festival (Apung Iru)
address: Pampanga River Bank & St. Peter Parish Church, Apalit, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Grand Fluvial River Parade (Libad) departs Apalit riverbank at 1:00 PM with hundreds of decorated boats.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Spectacular traditional fluvial river procession on the Pampanga River carrying the venerated ivory image of Saint Peter (Apung Iru) aboard a floating pagoda.
details: Devotees splash river water on passing boats to shower blessings, while brass bands play folk melodies on motorized bancas along the river.

name: Bacolor Lahar Historic Marker & Sunken Heritage Trail
address: Poblacion Heritage District, Bacolor, Pampanga
description: Historical monument and heritage marker honoring Bacolor as the former colonial capital of the Philippines and commemorating survival from the 1991 Mt. Pinatubo lahar.
details: Includes sunken plazas, exposed rooftops of buried houses, and heritage monuments depicting the heroic resilience and rebirth of the Kapampangan people.

name: Bale Matua (Founders Residence - 1824)
address: Santo Rosario St., Angeles City, Pampanga
description: The oldest surviving colonial residence in Angeles City, built in 1824 by town founders Don Angel Pantaleon de Miranda and Doña Rosalia de Jesus.
details: Preserved with high-ceiling timber columns, capiz shell lattice windows, and thick stone foundations that withstood multiple wars and colonial eras.

name: Batalla Festival (Masantol Sword Battle Pageant)
address: Masantol Parish Plaza & Coastal Poblacion Grounds, Masantol, Pampanga
eventDate: May 8 (Annual Feast of Saint Michael the Archangel)
scheduleNote: Solemn Archangel Mass at 8:00 AM; Dramatic theatrical Batalla sword fight reenactment at 2:00 PM; Evening coastal fluvial parade.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Centuries-old theatrical drama and folk dance pageant reenacting the legendary battle between the Archangel Saint Michael and celestial adversaries during the May town fiesta.
details: Devotees don shiny armor and vibrant capes, clashing wooden swords in stylized choreography passed down through coastal Kapampangan families for generations.

name: Betis Church - St. James the Apostle Parish Church
description: National Cultural Treasure known as the 'Sistine Chapel of the Philippines' for its stunning hand-painted wooden ceiling frescoes.
details: Built in 1660, features exquisite woodcarvings, ornate retablo, and historic belfry.

name: Betis Woodcarving (Dukit) Artisan Studios
address: Barangay Santa Ursula, Betis, Guagua, Pampanga
description: Centuries-old artisanal carving studios of Betis, known as the Woodcarving Capital of the Philippines, where master carvers fashion museum-grade baroque sculptures.
details: Visitors can watch master sculptors (mandudukit) hand-carve solid narra and molave into intricate ecclesiastical retablos, saints (santos), and heirloom furniture.

name: Candaba Bird Sanctuary & Wetlands
address: Barangay Paligui, Candaba, Pampanga
description: Internationally renowned wetland reserve that serves as a vital staging and wintering sanctuary for tens of thousands of migratory birds from Siberia, China, and Japan.
details: Vast 32,000-hectare freshwater marsh hosting rare avian species including purple swamphens, wild ducks, and egrets. Prime spot for eco-photographers and birdwatchers.

name: Caragan Festival
address: Mabalacat City Heroes Hall & Public Plaza, Mabalacat City, Pampanga
eventDate: Third to Fourth Week of February (February 18 - 25 Annual)
scheduleNote: Tribal Aeta street dance parade begins at 8:00 AM; Cultural indigenous craftsmanship exhibits and music performances at city plaza.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Vibrant indigenous festival honoring the first Aeta chieftain of Mabalacat, Garagan, showcasing the rich cultural heritage and tribal traditions of the Aeta indigenous community.
details: Features colorful indigenous costumes, headdresses, traditional archery contests, tribal dances, and celebration of indigenous identity.

name: Center for Kapampangan Studies Museum & Archives
address: Holy Angel University, Sto. Rosario St., Angeles City, Pampanga
description: Premier academic repository and museum preserving Kapampangan language, Kulitan calligraphy, archaeological treasures, ecclesiastical art, and rare recordings.
details: Features galleries dedicated to pre-colonial Kapampangan history, indigenous artifacts, traditional literature, and an interactive Kulitan writing station.

name: Dukit Festival (Betis Woodcarving Festival)
address: Betis District Heritage Center & St. James the Apostle Parish, Guagua, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Live on-the-spot master woodcarving competitions at 9:00 AM; Ecclesiastical wood sculpture exhibition open all day.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Celebrates Betis' renowned centuries-old ecclesiastical woodcarving (dukit) tradition, featuring live sculpting competitions where master carvers fashion intricate religious icons and heirloom furniture.
details: Known as the Woodcarving Capital of Central Luzon, Guagua honors the artisans of Betis whose baroque sculptures adorn churches and palaces worldwide.

name: Duman Festival
address: Santa Rita Heritage Church Plaza, Santa Rita, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Fresh Duman pounding demonstrations start at 3:00 PM. Evening cultural program and tasting banquet starts at 6:00 PM.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Celebrates the cherished Kapampangan culinary tradition of beating roasted young green glutinous rice (lakatan) into sweet, aromatic emerald-green flakes.
details: Duman is harvested exclusively during cooler November-December months. Served with hot Tsokolate de Batirol and traditional Santa Rita heirloom pastries.

name: Fiestang Kuliat & Sisig Festival
address: Heritage District & Crossing Sisig Strip, Angeles City, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Annual Sisig Cook-Off & Tasting Showcase from 4:00 PM onwards along the Heritage District.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: A month-long celebration honoring Angeles City's historical founding and its global prestige as the Sisig Capital of the Philippines.
details: Featuring massive sizzling plate demonstrations by master Kapampangan chefs, street parades, religious processions, and local craft markets.

name: Giant Lantern Festival (Ligligan Parul)
address: Robinsons Starmills / San Fernando Heritage District, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Grand Lantern Competition & Kaleidoscopic Light Exhibition runs nightly from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: World-famous Christmas spectacle where Pampanga master craftsmen build colossal 20-foot lanterns illuminated by over 10,000 dancing light bulbs synchronized to brass band music.
details: Celebrated since 1908, crowning San Fernando as the Christmas Capital of the Philippines. Each barangay competes with massive manually operated rotor mechanisms.

name: Holy Rosary Parish Church (Santo Rosario Church)
description: National Historical Landmark built in 1877 during the Spanish era using polo y servicio forced labor. Witnessed historic Philippine-American war events.
details: Features dual bell towers and magnificent stained glass windows overlooking Santo Rosario heritage district.

name: Ibun-Ebun Festival (Birds and Eggs Festival)
address: Candaba Swamp & Municipal Grounds, Candaba, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Early morning birdwatching tours at Candaba Sanctuary 6:00 AM - 9:00 AM. Salted egg culinary exhibitions held at town plaza.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Lively eco-cultural festival celebrating the Candaba Bird Sanctuary's migratory wild birds and the town's famed duck egg and salted egg (itlog na maalat) industries.
details: Street dancers wear magnificent bird wings and plumage. Features duck egg cracking tournaments and wetland conservation seminars.

name: Kamaru Festival (Camaru Cricket Festival)
address: Magalang Town Plaza & Municipal Heritage Grounds, Magalang, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Culinary Kamaru cook-off and cooking demonstrations at 10:00 AM; Street dancing competition and agro-trade fair throughout the day.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Unique culinary and agro-environmental fiesta celebrating Magalang's agricultural delicacy of mole crickets ('kamaru'), harvested from lush rice paddies at the foot of Mount Arayat.
details: Features street dancing with vibrant insect-themed costumes, cooking masterclasses for authentic Adobung Kamaru, and farm produce expos.

name: Lubao International Balloon & Music Festival
address: Pradera Verde, Prado Siongco, Lubao, Pampanga
eventDate: Late March to Early April (March 27 - 30 Annual)
scheduleNote: Morning hot air balloon ascent from 5:30 AM to 7:00 AM. Evening Balloon Night Glow and music concerts start at 6:00 PM.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Southeast Asia's largest hot air balloon spectacle, featuring dozens of international custom-shaped giant balloons, aerial shows, night concerts, and family outdoor festivities.
details: Held at the expansive 400-hectare Pradera Verde complex in Lubao with wakeboarding, golf, open-air food bazaars, and camping grounds.

name: Majigangga Festival (Fiesta da ring Majiganggas)
address: St. Anne Parish Church Plaza & Poblacion Heritage District, Santa Ana, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Majiganggas giant 14-foot papier-mâché puppet street dancing parade starts at 8:00 AM; Feast of Holy Innocents street spectacles; Christmas Lubenas lantern processions and evening cultural show at Santa Ana town plaza.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Enchanting folk festival celebrated every December in Santa Ana, featuring towering 10-to-14-foot giant papier-mâché puppets (called 'Majiganggas') with humorous, expressive faces dancing to lively brass band music through the streets during the Christmas season.
details: One of Pampanga's most beloved centuries-old Christmas folk traditions, dating back to the Spanish colonial era. Crafted using traditional bamboo frames and papier-mâché by Santa Ana artisans to bring joyous laughter, ward off evil spirits, and celebrate the holiday season.

name: Makatapak Festival (Barefoot Festival)
address: San Guillermo Sunken Church Grounds, Bacolor, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Barefoot procession walks across the lahar fields to San Guillermo Church at 6:30 AM.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Meaning 'Barefoot', this poignant cultural festival honors the Bacolor citizens who walked barefoot through volcanic mud and lahar to rebuild their town after Mt. Pinatubo erupted.
details: Townsfolk and visitors walk barefoot in unity, celebrating Kapampangan indomitable spirit, perseverance, and solidarity.

name: Metropolitan Cathedral of San Fernando (San Fernando Cathedral)
description: Seat of the Archdiocese of San Fernando, established in 1755.
details: Features a monumental dome and neo-classical stone facade overlooking the central municipal plaza.

name: Miyamit Falls & Porac Eco-Trail
address: Sapang Ubay, Barangay Diaz, Porac, Pampanga
description: Spectacular multi-tiered mountain waterfall cascading into a crystal basin within the ancestral domain of the indigenous Aeta community.
details: Surrounded by untouched tropical forests and dramatic rock formations in the foothills of Mt. Pinatubo; popular for 4x4 trails, trekking, and nature swimming.

name: Mount Arayat National Park & Tree House Trail
address: San Agustin Norte, Arayat, Pampanga
description: Protected ecological haven and volcanic sanctuary featuring natural mountain spring swimming pools, lush rainforest trails, and the legendary home of Maria Sinukuan.
details: Spanning over 3,715 hectares across solitary Mount Arayat, offering scenic views of Central Luzon, hiking trails, birdwatching, and refreshing volcanic spring baths.

name: Museo Ning Angeles (Museum of Angeles)
address: Heritage District, Santo Rosario St, Angeles City, Pampanga
description: Historic 1922 Angeles Municipal Hall transformed into a vibrant cultural museum housing the renowned Culinarium dedicated to Kapampangan culinary arts.
details: Showcases antique kitchen implements, heritage recipes, dioramas of traditional cooking methods, and historical exhibits commemorating the resilience of Angeles City.

name: Our Lady of Grace Parish Church (Mabalacat Church)
description: Historic Augustinian parish established in 1712, known for its distinct bell tower and brick entrance arches.
details: Preserves century-old wooden religious statues and Spanish-era parish records.

name: Pamintuan Mansion (Social History Museum)
address: Miranda St. corner Sto. Entierro St., Angeles City, Pampanga
description: Magnificent 1890s stone mansion that served as the seat of the First Philippine Republic under Gen. Emilio Aguinaldo and MacArthur’s headquarters.
details: Venue of the 1st Anniversary of the Philippine Declaration of Independence on June 12, 1899. Features a rooftop mirador watchtower, historic kitchen, and grand architecture.

name: Pyestang Tugak (San Fernando Frog Festival)
address: City Hall Grounds & Heritage District, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Frog culinary cook-offs and longest frog burger presentation at 10:00 AM. Betute Tugak tasting booths open all day.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: A uniquely lively culinary and environmental festival honoring the native farm frog (tugak) which controls rice field pests and inspires famous Kapampangan delicacies.
details: Features frog-catching competitions, frog mascot races, educational biodiversity exhibits, and tastings of authentic 'Betute' (deep-fried stuffed frog).

name: Sabuaga Festival (Shower of Petals)
address: Santo Tomas Town Plaza & Parish Church, Santo Tomas, Pampanga
eventDate: Easter Sunday (Annual March or April / Holy Week)
scheduleNote: Salubong dawn rites at 5:00 AM; Grand Sabuaga street dancing with petal showers along the main avenue at 8:00 AM.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Joyous Easter Sunday celebration derived from 'sabuag' (to scatter) and 'sampaga' (flowers), where thousands of dancers shower fresh flower petals to celebrate the Resurrection.
details: Santo Tomas, renowned as the pottery capital, combines clay craft artistry with flower-scattering dances in one of Pampanga's most uplifting religious festivals.

name: San Agustin Parish Church (Lubao Church)
description: The oldest church in Pampanga and Central Luzon, constructed in 1572 using brick, stone, and egg whites.
details: Important Cultural Property built by Fr. Antonio Herrera with massive 2-meter thick earthquake-proof walls.

name: San Bartolome Parish Church (Magalang Church)
description: Heritage parish church established in 1605 at the foot of Mount Arayat.
details: Features a grand symmetrical stone facade and historic baroque altarpiece.

name: San Fernando Giant Lantern (Parol) Artisan Workshop
address: Brgy. Del Pilar & San Jose, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
description: Master artisan studios where skilled lantern makers (paroleros) craft world-renowned illuminated kaleidoscopic Christmas lanterns using intricate mechanical rotors.
details: Showcases the historic craft of steel framing, papering, and wiring thousands of colored light bulbs that transform the city into the Christmas Capital of the Philippines.

name: San Fernando Train Station Museum
address: Brgy. Santo Niño, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
description: Colonial 1892 railway depot on the historic Manila-Dagupan line, famous as a stop of Dr. Jose Rizal and tragic final rail terminus of the 1942 Bataan Death March.
details: Restored brick station featuring authentic railway artifacts, bronze war memorial statues, vintage photographs, and historical exhibits.

name: San Guillermo Parish Church (Half-Buried Sunken Church)
description: Historic 16th-century church half-buried by 6-meter lahar mudflows from the 1991 Mt. Pinatubo eruption.
details: Visitors enter through the original upper window arches. Houses a fully restored gilded baroque retablo.

name: San Jose Obrero Parish Church (Floridablanca Church)
description: Heritage 19th-century parish church founded in 1823 under the patronage of Saint Joseph the Worker.
details: Built with traditional stone brick facade walls and a graceful octagonal bell tower.

name: San Luis Gonzaga Parish Church (San Luis Church)
description: Historic 18th-century riverside parish church overlooking the majestic Pampanga River bend.
details: Constructed in 1760 using volcanic tuff stone and traditional lime mortar.

name: San Miguel Arcangel Parish Church (Masantol Church)
description: Historic coastal parish church founded in 1877 under the patronage of Archangel Michael.
details: Overlooks the Pampanga river delta and historic fishing communities.

name: San Nicolas de Tolentino Parish Church (Candaba Church)
description: Historic Augustinian parish constructed in 1575, standing as the spiritual landmark of Candaba town center.
details: Features Neoclassical facade masonry and an octagonal multi-tiered belfry.

name: San Nicolas de Tolentino Parish Church (Macabebe Church)
description: Colonial Augustinian parish founded in 1575, featuring classic red brick facade masonry.
details: Renowned for its historic Spanish-era belfry overlooking coastal river delta routes.

name: San Pedro Cutud Lenten Rites (Maleldo)
address: Barangay San Pedro Cutud, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
eventDate: Good Friday / Holy Week (Annual March or April)
scheduleNote: Senakulo passion play starts at 10:00 AM. Solemn rites atop the Cutud Calvary hill culminate from 12:00 NN to 1:00 PM.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: World-famous traditional Holy Week passion play and solemn Lenten devotion where penitents reenact the journey and crucifixion of Jesus Christ.
details: Attracts international spectators, cultural researchers, and devout pilgrims. Visitors are encouraged to observe solemnity and dress respectfully.

name: Santa Ana Parish Church (Santa Ana Church)
description: Historic parish established in 1756 by Augustinian friars, featuring classic Spanish-colonial brick masonry.
details: Houses antique stone retablos and original century-old church bells.

name: Santa Catalina de Alejandria Parish Church (Arayat Church)
description: Colonial Augustinian parish established in 1590 at the foot of Mount Arayat under the patronage of St. Catherine of Alexandria.
details: Features a classic Renaissance-style facade and century-old brick bell tower.

name: Santa Catalina de Alejandria Parish Church (Porac Church)
description: Heritage 19th-century parish church founded in 1594 by Augustinian missionaries.
details: Restored after historic earthquake events, showcasing thick stone buttress walls.

name: Santa Lucia Parish Church (Sasmuan Church)
description: Historic coastal parish church founded in 1590, renowned for the miraculous Kuraldal healing dance festival.
details: Built over coastal wetlands, featuring massive stone walls and a single historic belfry.

name: Santa Monica Parish Church (Mexico Church)
description: Colonial Augustinian parish established in 1581, known for its historic belfry ruins.
details: Houses antique stone altars and century-old parish registers.

name: Santa Monica Parish Church (Minalin Sunken Church)
description: National Cultural Treasure built in 1614, featuring rare European-Moorish architectural motifs.
details: Renowned for its unique floral carvings, retablo-style facade, and ancient bamboo organ relics.

name: Santa Rita de Cascia Parish Church (Santa Rita Church)
description: Historic parish church founded in 1726, home to the sacred relic of Saint Rita of Cascia.
details: Features a large spacious nave, historic pipe organ loft, and century-old heritage trees.

name: Santo Tomas de Villanueva Parish Church (Santo Tomas Church)
description: Historic Augustinian parish church founded in 1792 in the pottery and palayok capital of Pampanga.
details: Stands as the spiritual heart of Santo Tomas, known for its solemn holy week traditions.

name: Santo Tomas Pottery & Clay Craft Center
address: Barangay Sto. Niño, Santo Tomas, Pampanga
description: Pampanga’s premier earthenware crafting hub where generations of local artisans mold clay pots (palayok), earthen cooking stoves (kalan), and garden terracotta.
details: Lined with traditional wood-fired kilns and open workshops where guests can try traditional foot-wheel pottery and take home handcrafted earthenware vessels.

name: Sasmuan Kuraldal Healing Festival
address: Santa Lucia Parish Church Plaza, Sasmuan, Pampanga
scheduleNote: Ecstatic brass band dance sessions held outside the church courtyard after morning and afternoon masses.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Ancient ecstatic healing dance festival where devotees from across the nation dance non-stop in the town plaza seeking fertility, cures for illness, and bountiful fishing harvests.
details: Dancers wave yellow handkerchiefs and chant 'Viva Santa Lucia! Puera Sakit!' (Away with sickness) in an extraordinary, spirited display of Kapampangan faith.

name: Sinukwan Festival
address: Heroes Hall & Capitol Boulevard Grounds, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
eventDate: Late November to Early December (November 28 - December 6 Annual)
scheduleNote: Street dancing parade begins at 7:30 AM along Capitol Boulevard; cultural trade fair and food exhibits open all day.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: Grand week-long cultural celebration honoring Aring Sinukwan, the mythological deity and guardian of Mount Arayat, featuring synchronized street dancing to 'Atin Cu Pung Singsing'.
details: Highlights the authentic indigenous Kapampangan spirit with vibrant feathered headdresses, traditional musical performances, trade fairs, and local delicacies.

name: St. Peter the Apostle Parish Church (Apalit Church)
description: Heritage parish founded in 1590, famous for the annual June Libad fluvial river procession honoring Apung Iru (St. Peter).
details: Built with thick brick masonry walls and features classical ceiling paintings.

name: Tigtigan Terakan Keng Dalan (TTKD Street Festival)
address: Balibago MacArthur Highway Entertainment Strip, Angeles City, Pampanga
eventDate: Last Friday & Saturday of October (October 24 - 26 Annual)
scheduleNote: MacArthur Highway pedestrian closure begins at 5:00 PM. Live music stages, food stalls, and dancing until 3:00 AM.
announcementNote: Wait for further announcements and updates here
description: The ultimate street party meaning 'Music and Dancing in the Streets', founded in 1992 to commemorate Angeles City's resilience and recovery from the 1991 Mt. Pinatubo eruption.
details: Features kilometers of open-air stages, sizzling Sisig grill bars, renowned Kapampangan and national bands, and tens of thousands of celebrants reveling in the streets.

name: Virgen del Pilar Parish Church (San Simon Church)
description: Historic Spanish colonial parish founded in 1771 under the patronage of Our Lady of the Pillar.
details: Features classic Renaissance facade arches and a historic bell tower overlooking MacArthur Highway.
